name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.8.1 — entry-point conformance: a new central manifest `spec/entrypoints.json` declares, per executable in `spec/scripts/*.js|*.sh` (excluding `spec/scripts/lib/`) and `spec/workflows/*.js`, which files invoke it, and `tests/consistency/entrypoints.test.js` diffs those declarations against the live repo in four directions on every `npm test` — inventory forward (a script with no entry, or an empty `entryPoints`, is red: there is no sanctioned orphan form), inventory reverse (a manifest key naming a missing file is red), invocation forward (a declared entry point that no longer carries the invocation literal is red), and invocation reverse (a `spec-paths <key>` or hooks.json call site the manifest does not declare is red); this closes the third recurrence of the authored-but-never-activated class (env-preflight absent from review was the third instance, closed in 7.7.0) with a deterministic guard per core § Incident Policy, its checker logic living in the test file as pure functions over an injectable root, exercised against the live repo as a green pin and against tmpdir fixtures for each red case so no red path is unfalsifiable. The guard's first catch, on the day it landed: `spec/scripts/advisory-append.js` is DELETED along with its `spec-paths advisory-append` key, its usage-line token, and `tests/advisory-append/` — its sole producer was the `wf-review` workflow's `smells` return, which v7 removed, leaving the script with no caller since (adjudicated by the user at build time). The reverse check considers only `spec-paths` keys resolving inside the executable inventory — nine live keys (`shared`, `shared-design`, `shared-genesis`, `replay-corpus`, `template`, `feedback-template`, `templates`, `contract`, `workflows`) resolve to doctrine files, templates, or directories and are not script invocations, so the domain is a glob-shape test rather than an on-disk listing and a stale case-table key pointing at a deleted script still surfaces instead of being silently swallowed. Deliberately out of scope: no `observed`-grammar declarations in the manifest (spec 03's executed pair test owns grammar liveness by execution), and no dynamic-invocation detection — an entry flagged `"dynamic": true` keeps only the file-existence check, and no entry needed that flag at seeding. The manifest is data about the plugin: no host contract change, no grounding-contract edit, no config key. Landing alongside the entry-point work, D13: `ac-matrix.js`'s `missing-test-file` check asserted existence for every `tests`-layer File Plan row regardless of the row's Action, so a spec that PLANS a test file's deletion produced a HARD finding by construction — surfaced by this spec's own D7 deletion row, the repo's first `tests`-layer DELETE. The check now exempts rows whose Action is `DELETE` and stays fail-closed everywhere else: an explicit `CREATE` naming a missing file still raises, and a row in a File Plan table that binds no Action column at all still raises. Pinned by a three-arm behavioral test so "fixed" cannot silently mean "disabled". 7.7.0 — review observation truth (2026-08-20 Salon OS field report): review-legs.js now runs the host's env preflight as a precondition before any leg, exiting 2 with stderr naming the unset declared vars and their provision commands and appending no manifest rows — closing the 3rd recurrence of the authored-not-activated class, where env-preflight.js was wired into build/design/doctor but absent from review; verdict.js's `deriveTestsSkipped` now types an unparseable skip observation as `testsSkipped: {"unavailable": true}` instead of silently deriving a fabricated `{total: 0}` CLEAN, and counts the `unavailable — skip format did not match gate output` gate row as one hard leg finding so silence about skips pages the same run it occurs — the sibling `unavailable — host runner declares no skip format` variant is a host's declared config state and raises nothing; promise-sweep.js gains an applicability cutoff (`APPLIES_FROM = '20260817'`, the date the carrier convention shipped, overridable via `--applies-from`) so specs locked before the convention existed emit a typed `not-applicable` manifest row instead of retroactive orphan noise, with undated paths applying the sweep in full (fail-closed); and a new executed producer→consumer pair test drives review-legs.js against synthetic hosts and feeds its ACTUAL emitted manifest to verdict.js, pinning the legs→verdict grammar end to end rather than against hand-written fixtures. 7.6.0 — replay scratch write access: `block-cross-worktree-writes.sh` now allows a cross-worktree Write/Edit whose TARGET tree's private git dir carries the `replay-worktree` marker AND has a `/worktrees/` segment — the mutation-authoring worker's sanctioned path into the replay scratch tree, closing the gap that had the first live run's worker blocked on Edit/Write and tunneling the same write through Bash — keyed on the target only, so a session anchored inside the scratch tree writing OUT to the main checkout still blocks, and every unmarked cross-worktree block, same-tree allow, and git/parse fail-open arm is unchanged; a same-day review-gate finding then caught the marker allow itself as forgeable — writes into a repo's `.git`-internal paths were already fail-open, so planting the marker into another tree's private git dir took two ordinary permitted Writes and no git access — closed by narrowing the marker allow to linked-worktree git dirs only (a top-level or out-of-band marker is never honoured) and by a new git-metadata attribution check that runs before the old fail-open: a target resolving inside THIS repo's own common git dir is attributed to its owning worktree and blocked unless that owner is the writing session's own tree, while a different repo's git metadata and genuine parse failures keep the prior fail-open; replay.md's Phase 1 setup gate now runs `git clean -fd` after its `git checkout -- .` restore, since checkout alone cannot remove files `setupCommand` *creates* (the same run left an untracked root `package-lock.json` that would have polluted the blind reviewer's tree) and clean cannot touch the marker living outside the working tree; and reviewer.md gains a return-contract section stating the verdict field's closed vocabulary (`CLEAN`/`REVIEWER_FAILED`) its consumers (`replay.js --score`, verdict.js) already enforce.
